event: Rooftop solar (distributed PV) growth: slow downward trend in NSW operational demand, strongest at midday and on mild sunny weekends/holidays (deepening 'duck curve'); NSW minimum demand fell from ~5,000+ MW (2019-2021) to 2,718 MW (Feb 2025). Distributed PV avg in NSW reached Q1 2026 record 1,338 MW and Q2 2026 record 865 MW. Offsetting upward drivers: data centres, electrification, home-battery charging (later rows).

Heatwave: NSW Q1 2019 maximum operational demand 13,821 MW (AEMO QED Q1 2019 Table 1; all-time NSW record 14,744 MW). WattClarity attributes the 13,821 MW peak to Thu 31 Jan 2019 (30-min operational demand). Not a record.

NSW daylight saving (Standard Time Act 1987): starts first Sunday in October 02:00 AEST->03:00 AEDT; ends first Sunday in April 03:00 AEDT->02:00 AEST. Transitions in span: end 2019-04-07; start 2019-10-06; end 2020-04-05; start 2020-10-04; end 2021-04-04; start 2021-10-03; end 2022-04-03; start 2022-10-02; end 2023-04-02; start 2023-10-01; end 2024-04-07; start 2024-10-06; end 2025-04-06; start 2025-10-05; end 2026-04-05; start 2026-10-04 (next end 2027-04-04). NEM time stays AEST (UTC+10) so during DST the NSW load profile (morning ramp and evening peak) appears one hour earlier in NEM-time data; daily energy roughly unchanged. Dates computed from the rule and checked against NSW Govt page (2026 start / 2027 end).

Recurring Easter (Good Friday-Easter Monday) and other NSW public holidays (New Year, Australia Day, Anzac Day, King's/Queen's Birthday, Labour Day, Christmas/Boxing Day plus substitute days). Holiday days have weekend-like demand; Easter dates move each year (2026: 3-6 Apr). Generic calendar effect.

Black Summer bushfires in NSW (state of emergency declared 11 Nov 2019; fires burned Sep 2019 to Feb 2020; end date approximate, not verified). Bushfire-related transmission outages (e.g. 30 Dec 2019 VIC-NSW interconnector flows reversed; 4 Jan 2020 NSW-VIC separation). Smoke and heat raise cooling load; line outages are supply-side. Demand effect mixed/localised.
announced: 2019-11-11 NSW Premier state of emergency (search-confirmed only)

event: Recurring Christmas-New Year shutdown (roughly 24 Dec-2 Jan each year): commercial/industrial load drops; low weekday demand and deep midday minima (e.g. NSW Q4 low 29 Dec 2025). Generic annual seasonal effect - model as calendar covariate, not a changepoint.

Extreme heat plus bushfires: Penrith 48.9 C (highest known Sydney-basin temperature). Bushfires tripped southern NSW lines, separating NEM into north/south islands for just under 7 h; actual LOR2 in NSW, RERT used (~$8m), NSW price $14,700/MWh for 1 h. Tomago smelter switched off potlines in response to prices (operational demand lowered by price response). Heat pushes demand up; separation is supply-side.
announced: Forecast heat/LOR notices in advance; separation unannounced (fault)

event: East-coast heatwave: NEM daily max operational demand 35,440 MW on 31 Jan 2020 (NEM all-time record); NSW Q1 2020 max 13,835 MW (QED Table 1; WattClarity attributes it to Sat 1 Feb 2020). Five coal units offline; SA-VIC separation 13:24 on 31 Jan (towers down in western VIC, supply-side) left low reserves in NSW/VIC; actual LOR2 in NSW, RERT activated; NSW prices >$12,000/MWh for 90 min; Tomago potlines switched off (price-driven demand reduction).
announced: Forecast LOR notices on the day; separation unannounced

event: COVID-19: Public Health (COVID-19 Places of Social Gathering) Order 2020 closes pubs, clubs, gyms, entertainment and indoor recreation venues from 12 noon 23 Mar 2020 (NSW Gazette No 54).
announced: Order dated 23 Mar 2020 (national cabinet stage 1 announced 22 Mar 2020; not separately verified)

event: COVID-19 NSW stay-at-home Public Health Order (Restrictions on Gathering and Movement) Order 2020: made 30 Mar 2020, commences start of 31 Mar 2020; must not leave home without reasonable excuse; 2-person gathering limit. Replaced by eased Order (No 2) from 15 May 2020. [This dataset, rough weather/calendar-adjusted daily model: NSW TOTALDEMAND about -400 MW (-5.7%) late Mar-Apr 2020, about -170 to -310 MW (-2 to -4%) May-Jun 2020; consistent with AEMO QED.]

AEMO QED Q2 2020: COVID-19 cut NEM operational demand ~2.1% (483 MW); NSW and QLD most affected. NSW COVID-related decrease largest in April (-5% on average, strict restrictions all month), easing to about -1% by June. NSW Q2 2020 operational demand -192 MW vs Q2 2019 (underlying -109 MW, PV -83 MW).

COVID-19 easing: Public Health (COVID-19 Restrictions on Gathering and Movement) Order (No 2) 2020 commences start of 15 May 2020 (cafes/restaurants/pubs up to 10 diners, 5 home visitors). Further easing 1 Jun 2020 to 50 patrons (news reports only, not verified in gazette).
announced: Order dated 14 May 2020 (easing announced ~10 May 2020, not verified)

event: NSW Electricity Infrastructure Roadmap released (9 Nov 2020); Electricity Infrastructure Investment Bill introduced 10 Nov 2020, assented Dec 2020. Long-run supply/transmission policy; no short-run demand effect expected.
announced: 2020-11-09 NSW Govt announcement (date from search results; source opened confirms 10 Nov bill introduction)

event: Callide C (QLD) fire/explosion: auxiliary supply lost 13:33, fault at 14:06 tripped Calvale substation; ~3,045 MW scheduled generation lost, QNI tripped (QLD temporarily separated ~16 s), under-frequency load shedding mainly in QLD (>1 million people lost power up to ~2 h). AEMO report says UFLS relays in QLD and NSW disconnected distribution circuits (~359 MW DPV lost) - possible small, brief NSW dip; otherwise NSW demand not expected to change. Report too large to open in full; facts from AEMO report excerpts.
announced: Unannounced fault; AEMO preliminary report 2 Jun 2021, final report 15 Oct 2021

event: COVID-19 Greater Sydney lockdown: 4 LGAs (City of Sydney, Waverley, Woollahra, Randwick) stay-at-home from 23:59 Fri 25 Jun 2021; extended to all Greater Sydney incl. Blue Mountains, Central Coast, Wollongong (later Shellharbour) from 18:00 Sat 26 Jun 2021; repeatedly extended; stay-at-home lifted for fully vaccinated from Mon 11 Oct 2021 (70% double-dose milestone). [This dataset: about -130 MW (-1.4%) in Jul 2021 and about -210 MW (-2.8%) Aug to 11 Oct 2021 vs adjusted model; smaller than 2020 and within the daily noise (residual sd ~400 MW), so visible only as a sustained shift.]
announced: 2021-06-26 NSW Health release ('from 6pm today'); 4-LGA order announced 25 Jun 2021; reopening roadmap 9 Sep 2021

event: AEMO QED Q3 2021: strict NSW COVID restrictions plus mild Aug/Sep weather cut NSW underlying demand 72 MW (avg) vs Q3 2020; operational demand fell sharply after July (-359 MW vs Aug-Sep 2020). NSW Q3 max 12,423 MW (cold early July, highest Q3 since 2011); NSW min 4,872 MW at 12:30 Sun 19 Sep 2021 (lowest since Q1 2000).

COVID-19 regional NSW stay-at-home orders (whole state) from 17:00 Sat 14 Aug 2021 (initially to 00:01 22 Aug; extended). Many regional areas exited at midnight Fri 10 Sep 2021 (mid-north coast, north coast, Albury, Riverina, Murrumbidgee); others stayed locked down to 11 Oct 2021.
announced: 2021-08-14 ~14:26 Deputy Premier tweet, ~15:45 Premier confirmation (The New Daily), effective 17:00 - under 3 h notice

event: NEM five-minute settlement (5MS) commenced 1 Oct 2021 (delayed from 1 Jul 2021). Market settlement change only; NSW demand not expected to change (dispatch was already 5-minute). Possible artefact risk if mixing 30-min and 5-min price/demand series.
announced: AEMC rule 2017; delay determined 9 Jul 2020 (search-confirmed; AEMC page not opened, 403)

event: AGL announces Bayswater (2,640 MW, NSW black coal) to close no later than 2033 (previously 2035); window 2030-2033. Supply-side; NSW demand not expected to change.

Origin notifies AEMO of potential early retirement of Eraring (2,880 MW, largest NEM coal plant) in Aug 2025 (previously 2032). Superseded 2024 and 2026 (see later rows). Supply-side; demand not expected to change.
announced: 2022-02-17 Origin ASX half-year results / AEMO closure notice

event: Liddell Unit 3 retired at start of Q2 2022 (first of 4 Liddell units). Combined Bayswater+Liddell June 2022 output record low. Supply-side; demand not expected to change.

Very cold start to winter 2022 on the east coast (coldest start to June in decades for many cities). NSW daily peak operational demand 12,141 MW on 14 Jun 2022 (~500 MW above day-ahead forecast). Coincides with the June 2022 market crisis (next rows). Span approximate.

June 2022 NEM crisis - administered pricing: QLD APP from TI 18:55 12 Jun; NSW APP from TI 18:35 13 Jun 2022 (cumulative price threshold breached), SA 22:00 and VIC 22:05 13 Jun; NSW APP ended TI 04:00 23 Jun. ~300 MW RERT dispatched NSW 14 Jun 18:05-21:05. Market/supply event. Demand effect small and two-way: before APP high prices caused ~630 MW (10 Jun, NSW+VIC) and ~300 MW (12-13 Jun, NSW) industrial load reductions; under capped prices that response weakened; RERT/DNSP/voluntary reductions lowered demand 14-18 Jun. No involuntary load shedding.
announced: APP triggered automatically by CPT; forecast LOR2 MN 97365 (14 Jun)

event: AEMO suspends NEM spot market in all regions from TI 14:05 15 Jun 2022 (MN 97705, NER 3.14.3(a)(3)); market suspension pricing schedule applied. Forecast LOR3 NSW 15 Jun (MN 97776) -> ~489 MW RERT in NSW 17:30-23:30 15 Jun; ~463 MW RERT NSW 20:00 17 Jun-04:10 18 Jun. Dispatch pricing resumed TI 04:05 23 Jun; suspension formally ended 14:00 24 Jun 2022 (MN 99369 issued ~10:00 24 Jun). No involuntary load shedding. NSW demand not expected to change materially (cold weather simultaneous; RERT shaved some evening peaks). [This dataset: no demand change attributable to the suspension; adjusted daily residual 12-24 Jun 2022 about -25 MW (-0.3%), while raw demand was high because of the cold weather (late May-mid June). Market event, not a demand changepoint.]
announced: MN 97705 at 14:05 AEST 15 Jun 2022; staged lifting criteria published 22 Jun; MN 99369 ~10:00 24 Jun

event: One-off NSW public holiday: National Day of Mourning for Queen Elizabeth II (Thu 22 Sep 2022). Expect holiday-like weekday demand reduction.
announced: Announced ~11-12 Sep 2022; order published 13 Sep 2022 (search-confirmed; legislation PDF not opened, 403)

event: Sydney WorldPride 2023 (17 Feb-5 Mar; Mardi Gras parade Sat 25 Feb). Large public event; visible state-level demand effect unlikely.
Liddell Power Station fully closed: remaining three units decommissioned 24, 26 and 28 Apr 2023 (avg Liddell output -482 MW in Q2 2023). Supply-side; NSW demand not expected to change.
announced: Pre-announced years ahead (AGL); final units 24/26/28 Apr 2023

event: Vales Point B (1,320 MW, Delta Electricity) expected closure moved from 2029 to 2033 in AEMO Generation Information update. Supply-side; demand not expected to change.
announced: 2023-07-13 AEMO Generator Expected Closure Year update

event: FIFA Women's World Cup semi-final Matildas v England, Stadium Australia Sydney, 20:00 Wed 16 Aug 2023; most-watched Australian TV program since 2001 (peak reach 11.15m, avg 7.13m). Possible small evening load-shape anomaly; state-level effect unlikely to be visible.
NSW all-time minimum operational demand 3,719 MW at 12:00 Sun 29 Oct 2023 (previous all-time low 4,101 MW on Sun 24 Sep 2023); distributed PV 53.7% of underlying demand.

Data-centre load growth (mainly Sydney): NSW data-centre demand averaged 398 MW in Q1 2026 (+18% y/y) and 451 MW in Q2 2026 (+35% y/y); AEMO cites data centres, electrification and population as underlying-demand drivers. 11 data centres (5.4 GW) in AEMO connection pipeline Q1 2026, 17 (9.0 GW) Q2 2026 (NEM-wide). Slow upward trend, flat-profile load.
Severe storm in Victoria destroyed transmission towers/lines and caused generation outages; VIC/TAS price volatility. Victorian event - NSW demand not expected to change.

NSW high-demand day: demand surged above 13,000 MW at peak (AEMO); WattClarity: 30-min operational demand peak 13,643 MW (HH ending 17:00), not a record. VNI export constraints; $17m positive IRSR into NSW.
NSW Q1 minimum operational demand 4,449 MW at 12:00 Sat 30 Mar 2024 (Easter Saturday) - PV plus public-holiday effect.

Origin and NSW Government agree (Generator Engagement Project Agreement) to delay Eraring closure to 19 Aug 2027 (state underwriting; must retire fully by Apr 2029). Supply-side; demand not expected to change.
announced: 2024-05-23 Origin ASX release / NSW Govt announcement

event: AEMO Integrating Energy Storage Systems (IESS) rule commences: grid batteries register as bidirectional units (BDUs). AEMO 'Demand Terms in EMMS Data Model' v16.0 (3 Jun 2024) defines Total Demand (TOTALDEMAND) as excluding the local demand of scheduled loads and scheduled BDUs, so battery and pumped-hydro charging is excluded both before (as scheduled loads) and after; low risk of a definitional break, but worth checking around this date.
announced: Rule made 2021 (AEMC ERC0280); commencement known in advance

event: Commonwealth Energy Bill Relief Fund: NSW households $300 rebate 2024-25 (quarterly $75 credits from 1 Jul 2024), extension $150 for Jul-Dec 2025. Bill credit, not a price signal - no measurable demand effect expected.
announced: Federal Budget 14 May 2024; extension in 2025-26 Budget (Mar 2025)

event: Polar cold snap: NEM winter maximum operational demand record 33,381 MW (HH ending 18:30 15 Jul 2024); NSW Q3 2024 max up 1,057 MW (+9%) y/y, the largest regional increase (implied NSW Q3 2024 max ~12,565 MW from Q3 2025 report; exact NSW date not stated).
NSW all-time minimum operational demand 3,555 MW at 13:00 Sat 21 Sep 2024.
NSW all-time minimum operational demand 3,121 MW at 13:00 Sat 26 Oct 2024 (-434 MW vs 21 Sep 2024); same day NEM all-time minimum 10,073 MW at 11:30.

NSW heatwave (up to 39 C in parts of Sydney): peak operational demand >11,000 MW, >2,000 MW above November peaks of prior 3 years (forecast >12,000 MW); 4 coal units + 1 gas unit offline; price at MPC $17,500/MWh 14:30-15:35. Forecast LOR2/LOR3 declared up to 5 days ahead; forecast LOR3 MN 121021 (07:27); actual LOR2 from 15:30 then downgraded to actual LOR1; 605 MW short-notice RERT contracted, 184 MW pre-activated, 65 MWh activated. No involuntary load shedding.
announced: Forecast LOR3/LOR2 market notices from ~22 Nov 2024; MN 121021 07:27 27 Nov 2024

event: NSW all-time minimum operational demand 2,718 MW at 12:00 Sun 16 Feb 2025 (previous all-time 3,121 MW, 26 Oct 2024); still the NSW all-time low as of the latest QED checked (Q2 2026).

Late-summer heat: NSW operational demand 12,039 MW (HH ending 17:30) on 15 Mar 2025, 144 MW below the NSW Q1 2025 maximum recorded the next day (~12,183 MW implied); Collector-Marulan outage cut VNI northward flow to 0 MW; NSW >$14,000/MWh for 5 intervals.

Cold June 2025: NEM Q2 max 32,681 MW (HH ending 18:30 16 Jun 2025, highest Q2 since 2007); NSW Q2 max up 371 MW (+3.1%) y/y, occurring in June (exact NSW figure/date not stated); VIC winter record 8,818 MW on 25 Jun.

Commonwealth Cheaper Home Batteries Program starts 1 Jul 2025 (~30% discount via STCs). AEMO QED Q2 2026: rising home-battery charging (with industrial/data-centre load) lifted daytime operational demand and lowered evening peaks across most regions. Expect gradual midday-up / evening-down shape change, not a step.
announced: Announced as election commitment (Feb-Mar 2025, not verified); program start 1 Jul 2025

event: Cold winter 2025 (record low temperatures in parts of NSW mid-late July and August): NSW Q3 2025 maximum operational demand 13,204 MW, highest Q3 since 2008 (exact date not stated in QED). NSW Q3 2025 minimum 3,265 MW at 12:00 21 Sep 2025 (new Q3 low).

Tomago Aluminium (NSW's largest load, ~850 MW, ~10-12% of NSW electricity) begins staff consultation on possible closure at end-2028 when its AGL power contract expires; Rio Tinto says no decision made. No current demand change; a closure would be a ~850 MW step-down after 2028. Note Tomago does curtail potlines in price spikes (e.g. 4 and 31 Jan 2020).

Cloud over Sydney late morning cut rooftop PV output and sent NSW market demand up, prices to the market price cap for four intervals (~11:00-11:15 NEM time), then demand fell back (this dataset: TOTALDEMAND ~9,000 MW at 12:10 to ~6,350 MW by 13:05, RRP to -1,000 $/MWh). Illustrates large intra-day demand swings from behind-the-meter solar; no daily-level shift.

Federal Government (PM Albanese) announces rescue effort with NSW to keep Tomago open beyond 2028 (long-term fixed-price energy supply; Tomago to invest >=A$1bn). No demand change; removes the post-2028 closure risk if finalised.

NSW Q4 minimum operational demand 2,848 MW at 12:30 29 Dec 2025 (holiday period plus PV; Q4 low, not all-time). Same quarter: NEM all-time minimum 9,666 MW at 12:00 Sat 4 Oct 2025; NSW Q4 2025 max 13,022 MW.

NSW heatwave (>40 C in parts of Sydney): operational demand above 13,000 MW at start of evening price spike; prices >$10,000/MWh in 9 intervals 18:35-19:20; Avon-Marulan outage, QNI/VNI constraints. (NEM Q1 2026 max 33,645 MW on 7 Jan 2026.)

Origin extends Eraring: all four units to run from 19 Aug 2027 to 30 Apr 2029 (citing AEMO Transition Plan for System Security); no further major overhauls. Supply-side; demand not expected to change.

Federal and NSW governments announce ~A$2.5bn joint package (NSW capped at A$1.225bn over a decade from 2029) to keep Tomago operating beyond 2028; owners invest >=A$1.1bn; ~3 GW new renewables. No demand change; Tomago (~590 kt/yr, ~a tenth of NSW electricity use) stays as baseload.
